_source: Company tags come from public candidate reports (systemdesign.io question list, Oct 2026). Empty means no public source yet.

reqF: Shorten a long URL to a 7-character code
Redirect a code to the original URL
reqN: Very read heavy: 100 reads per write
Highly available: a dead link is a broken promise
est: Storage: 100M x 500 B x 365 x 5 yr ≈ 90 TB
Cache: top 20% of daily reads ≈ a few hundred GB
data: urls: code PK, long_url, user_id, created_at, expires_at
Key-value store partitioned by code
clicks: append-only events to Kafka, rolled up in the warehouse

blocks.u: Start from the people clicking links: almost all traffic is redirects.
blocks.lb: Spreads redirect traffic across stateless API servers.
blocks.api: Stateless service: creates codes and serves redirects.
blocks.id: Hands out unique 64-bit ids; base62 of the id is the code, so no collisions.
blocks.c: Hot codes live in Redis: most redirects never touch the DB.
blocks.db: Key-value store, partitioned by code: one lookup per miss.
blocks.k: Click events go to a queue so redirects stay fast.
blocks.w: Analytics runs offline on the warehouse, not on the hot path.

dives: How do you generate codes without collisions?
A Snowflake-style id generator, then base62. 7 chars = 3.5 trillion codes. No check-and-retry needed.
301 is cached by browsers (fewer hits, no click tracking). 302 every time (lets you count clicks).
How do you keep redirects under 50 ms?
Cache hot codes (80/20 rule), CDN or edge for the top links, KV store sharded by code.
Custom aliases?
Check-and-set insert on the alias; reject if taken.
wrap: Bottleneck: the KV store on cache misses. Fix: bigger cache, read replicas.
Abuse: rate limit creation per user, scan for malicious URLs.
Next: expiry cleanup job, analytics dashboards.

reqF: Limit requests per user, IP or API key
Return 429 with Retry-After when over the limit
reqN: Fails open if the limiter is down
est: 10M active keys x ~100 B ≈ 1 GB of counters
One Redis round trip per request: shard Redis by key
data: counters in Redis: key = rule:user:window → count, TTL
rules: id, match (path, method), limit, window, scope

blocks.u: Clients of every kind hit one front door.
blocks.gw: The limiter lives in the gateway so every service is protected.
blocks.s: Allowed requests pass straight to the services.
blocks.r: Shared counters in Redis, updated atomically with a Lua script.
blocks.cfg: Rules come from config, so limits change without a deploy.
blocks.x: Over the limit: 429 plus Retry-After, so clients back off.

dives: Which algorithm?
Token bucket: allows short bursts, simple, most common. Sliding window counter if you need smoother limits.
How do you stay correct across many gateways?
Central Redis with an atomic Lua script (INCR + check + EXPIRE in one step).
What if Redis is down?
Fail open with a local in-memory fallback limit, and alert.
Hot keys?
Shard counters by key; keep a local token cache for very hot clients.
wrap: Bottleneck: Redis round trip. Fix: local batching, shard by key.
Next: per-plan limits, dashboards of who is throttled.

reqN: Delivery under 200 ms when both are online
Messages never lost, kept in order per chat
est: Open connections: ~100M at peak, ~50k per server ≈ 2k servers
data: messages: chat_id (partition), msg_id (sort), sender, body, ts
chats + members tables
presence in Redis with TTL heartbeats

blocks.a: User A on a phone with a long-lived connection.
blocks.b: User B, maybe on another server or offline.
blocks.w1: WebSocket servers keep open connections for 2-way realtime.
blocks.w2: Each user is pinned to one chat server.
blocks.k: The queue routes messages between servers and absorbs bursts.
blocks.p: Presence lives in Redis with heartbeats and TTLs.
blocks.db: Cassandra: partition by chat, sort by message id, fast writes.
blocks.push: Offline users get a push, then sync when they reconnect.
blocks.s3: Media goes to object storage and a CDN, not through chat servers.

dives: How do you keep order?
Per-chat sequence ids assigned on write; clients sort by them.
How do you avoid duplicates?
Client message id = idempotency key; server dedupes.
Group chat with 500 members?
Fan out through the queue; big groups use pull on open.
How do you know who is online?
Heartbeats every ~30 s into Redis with a TTL.
wrap: Bottleneck: connection servers. Fix: scale horizontally, a registry of user → server.
Next: end-to-end encryption, message search.

reqF: See a feed of people you follow, newest or ranked
reqN: A new post can take a few seconds to appear
data: posts: post_id, author_id, body, media, created_at
follows: follower_id, followee_id
feed cache: user_id → list of post ids

blocks.u: Readers open the feed far more than they post.
blocks.gw: Auth and routing for posts and feed reads.
blocks.k: New-post events decouple writing from fan-out.
blocks.fo: Workers push the post id into each follower's feed.
blocks.g: Who follows whom, read by the fan-out workers.
blocks.fc: Each feed is a Redis list of post ids, ready to read.
blocks.cdn: Images and video come from the CDN.

dives: Fan-out on write or read?
Write for most users (fast reads). Read-time pull for celebrities. Merge both: hybrid.
Why store ids, not posts, in the feed?
Small lists; hydrate post details from cache at read time.
Pagination?
Cursor based (last post id), never offset.
Ranking?
A ranking service scores candidates; start with recency.
wrap: Bottleneck: fan-out for big accounts. Fix: hybrid fan-out.
Next: ranking model, ads insertion, notifications.

reqF: Watch with smooth playback on any device
reqN: Huge egress: CDN serves almost everything
est: Each video stored in ~6 renditions ≈ 5x raw size
Egress: millions of concurrent streams x ~5 Mbps ≈ Tbps, so CDN
data: videos: id, owner, title, status, renditions
segments in object storage: /video/rendition/segment.ts

blocks.up: Hands out pre-signed URLs so uploads go straight to storage.
blocks.raw: Raw uploads land in object storage.
blocks.q: Each upload becomes a transcode job.
blocks.tr: Workers split, encode many bitrates and merge.
blocks.cdn: The CDN serves the bytes, close to viewers.
blocks.v: Viewers stream segments and switch quality on the fly.
blocks.api: Video API serves the watch page and manifest.
blocks.meta: Metadata DB: titles, status, view counts.

dives: Why pre-signed uploads?
Big files skip your servers; resumable multipart upload to S3.
Adaptive bitrate?
Client picks the next segment's quality from measured bandwidth.
How do you transcode fast?
Split into chunks, encode in parallel as a DAG, merge.
Cost of egress?
CDN with high hit ratio, pre-warm popular videos at the edge.
wrap: Bottleneck: transcode backlog. Fix: autoscale workers, prioritise popular creators.
Next: recommendations, live streaming.

reqF: Pay at the end of the trip
reqN: A driver is never offered two trips at once
est: Location data is small and short-lived: keep it in memory
api: WS: driver location updates, ride status pushes
data: trips: id, rider, driver, status, route, fare
driver locations: in-memory geo index (H3 / geohash)

blocks.r: Riders request trips and watch the car arrive.
blocks.d: Drivers stream their location every few seconds.
blocks.t: Trip service owns the ride lifecycle.
blocks.l: Location service ingests 250k updates per second.
blocks.m: Matching finds and locks the best nearby driver.
blocks.geo: In-memory geo index for nearby search.
blocks.tdb: Trips DB: durable record of every ride.
blocks.maps: Maps and ETA service for routes and arrival times.
blocks.pay: Payment runs when the trip ends.

dives: Why not store locations in a database?
250k writes/s of data that expires in seconds: keep it in memory (Redis GEO / H3 cells).
How do you find nearby drivers?
Look up the rider's cell and its neighbours, then rank by ETA.
How do you avoid double booking a driver?
Lock the driver (atomic set with TTL) while the offer is open.
What if a region's servers fail?
Partition by city; failover per region.
wrap: Bottleneck: location ingest. Fix: shard by geo cell.
Next: surge pricing, pooled rides.

reqN: One slow channel never blocks the others
data: preferences: user, channel, opt_in, quiet_hours
device_tokens: user, platform, token
log: id, status, timestamps

blocks.s: Any service can trigger a notification.
blocks.n: One service validates, applies preferences and renders templates.
blocks.pref: Preferences and device tokens decide where it can go.
blocks.tpl: Templates keep copy out of code.
blocks.q1: A queue per channel isolates failures.
blocks.q3: SMS is slow and costly, so it is isolated.
blocks.w: Workers send, retry with backoff, then DLQ.

dives: How do you avoid duplicates?
Idempotency key per notification; workers check before sending.
What if a provider is down?
Retry with backoff, then dead-letter queue; failover to a second provider.
Quiet hours?
Delay into a scheduled queue by user time zone.
Rate limits?
Per-user caps so nobody gets spammed.
wrap: Bottleneck: provider limits. Fix: per-channel throttling, multiple providers.
Next: digesting, A/B tests on copy.

reqF: Crawl the web from seed URLs
Re-crawl pages to keep them fresh
reqN: Robust to traps and bad HTML
est: URL frontier: billions of URLs on disk
data: url seen set (Bloom filter + store)
content: url hash → compressed HTML in S3
frontier: priority queues per host

blocks.seed: Start from a list of seed URLs.
blocks.f: The frontier decides what to fetch next, by priority and politeness.
blocks.dns: A cached DNS resolver avoids a slow lookup per page.
blocks.cs: Raw pages go to object storage.
blocks.dd: A Bloom filter drops URLs already seen.
blocks.seen: The durable set of seen URLs.

dives: How are you polite?
One queue per host, a delay between requests, obey robots.txt.
Duplicates?
URL dedupe with a Bloom filter; content dedupe with simhash.
Crawler traps?
Max depth, URL length limits, per-site page caps.
Freshness?
Re-crawl by page change rate and importance.
wrap: Bottleneck: DNS and network. Fix: DNS cache, more fetchers per region.
Next: JavaScript rendering, ranking signals.

reqN: Never lose a payment: strong consistency
Reconciled with the provider every day
est: 1M payments/day ≈ 12/s average, 100x peaks on sale days
Small data, high stakes: correctness over speed
data: payments: id, order_id, amount, status (state machine), idempotency_key UNIQUE
ledger_entries: account, debit, credit, payment_id (append-only)

blocks.co: Checkout creates the order and calls payments.
blocks.pdb: Payments DB holds the state machine.
blocks.wh: Webhooks confirm results from the provider.
blocks.led: Double-entry ledger: every debit has a credit.
blocks.rec: Daily reconciliation against the provider's settlement file.

dives: How do you never charge twice?
Idempotency key with a UNIQUE constraint; retries return the first result.
What states can a payment be in?
CREATED → PENDING → SUCCEEDED / FAILED, only forward.
Why a ledger?
Append-only double-entry: balances always add up and are auditable.
What if the webhook never arrives?
Poll the provider for pending payments; reconcile daily.
wrap: Bottleneck: provider latency. Fix: async confirmation via webhooks.
Next: multi-currency, payouts, chargebacks.

reqF: Show top 5 suggestions as the user types
reqN: Suggestions can be an hour stale
est: Unique prefixes: hundreds of millions; top-k cached per prefix fits in memory per shard
data: trie: prefix → top-k completions (in memory, snapshot to store)
query logs → hourly counts

blocks.tc: In-memory trie with top-k cached at each node.
blocks.ts: Trie snapshots in storage, loaded at start.
blocks.log: Every query is logged to a stream.
blocks.tb: Builds a fresh trie offline and swaps it in.

dives: Why cache top-k per node?
Lookup becomes O(prefix length), no tree walk at query time.
How do you update?
Rebuild offline from logs and swap atomically.
Scale?
Shard by prefix range; replicate hot shards.
Client tricks?
Debounce typing, cache in the browser.
wrap: Bottleneck: hot prefixes like 'a'. Fix: replicate, cache at the edge.
Next: personalisation, multiple languages.

est: 50M users x 10 GB ≈ 500 PB raw, dedupe saves a lot
data: files: id, path, owner, version, chunk_list
chunks: hash → storage location (deduped)

blocks.c: The desktop client watches folders and splits files into chunks.
blocks.bs: Block service accepts only the chunks that changed.
blocks.mdb: SQL for metadata: versions need strong consistency.
blocks.nt: Other devices are told something changed.
blocks.o: Other devices pull only the new chunks.

dives: Why chunk files?
Upload only changed 4 MB chunks; dedupe identical chunks by hash.
Conflicts?
Version check on commit; on conflict keep both copies.
Why SQL for metadata?
Transactions for versions and paths.
How do devices find out?
Long poll or WebSocket notifications, then fetch changes.
wrap: Bottleneck: metadata DB. Fix: shard by user or namespace.
Next: sharing permissions, LAN sync.

est: Hot event: 1M users for 50k seats in minutes
data: seats: event_id, seat_id, status, UNIQUE (event, seat)
holds in Redis with TTL
bookings: id, user, seats, status

blocks.wr: A virtual waiting room lets people in at a safe rate.
blocks.ev: Event service: details and seat maps.
blocks.bk: Booking service runs hold, pay, confirm.
blocks.lk: Seat holds in Redis with a 10-minute TTL.
blocks.bdb: Bookings in SQL with a unique constraint as the last guard.

dives: How do you prevent double booking?
Hold with SET NX EX in Redis, plus a UNIQUE (event, seat) in the DB.
What happens if payment fails?
The hold expires or is released; the seat returns.
Flash sale?
Waiting room, cached event pages, admit in batches.
Fairness?
Queue position by arrival, block bots.
wrap: Bottleneck: seat-hold contention. Fix: shard holds by section.
Next: resale, dynamic pricing.

reqN: New places can take a day to appear
data: places: id, name, lat, lng, geohash, category
geo index: geohash cell → place ids

blocks.ls: Location search turns a point into cells and finds places.
blocks.c: Cache of place details for fast results.

dives: How do you search a radius?
Find the geohash cell for the point plus its 8 neighbours, then filter by distance.
Geohash or quadtree?
Geohash is simple; a quadtree adapts to dense cities.
Freshness?
Rebuild the index nightly; edits are rare.
Scale reads?
Replicas and cache; the index fits in memory.
wrap: Bottleneck: dense cells downtown. Fix: longer geohash or quadtree.
Next: ranking by rating and distance.

reqF: Chat with an AI model, answers stream in
Pick the right model for the job
est: ~1k tokens per turn ≈ 20B tokens/day: cost is the key number
data: conversations, messages (role, content, tokens, model)
usage per user per day

blocks.cs: Chat service streams tokens back over SSE.
blocks.r: The router picks a model by cost and latency.
blocks.sc: Semantic cache answers repeated questions cheaply.
blocks.llm: Hosted model API for the hard questions.
blocks.sh: Self-hosted model for cheap, high volume.
blocks.ob: Tracing and evals: latency, cost, quality.

dives: How do you stream?
Server-Sent Events from the chat service, token by token.
Long conversations?
Trim or summarise old turns to fit the context window.
Cost control?
Route easy prompts to small models, cache, limit tokens per user.
Provider outage?
Fallback to another provider through the router.
wrap: Bottleneck: model latency and cost. Fix: routing, caching, smaller models.
Next: tools, memory, RAG.

reqF: Stay up to date as documents change
reqN: Grounded: say 'not found' instead of guessing
est: 1M documents ≈ 20M chunks x 1.5 KB vectors ≈ 30 GB index
data: chunks: id, doc_id, text, embedding, acl, updated_at
BM25 keyword index alongside vectors

blocks.ch: Load and split into chunks with overlap.
blocks.rag: RAG service runs the pipeline per question.
blocks.rr: A reranker keeps the best 5 of 50.
blocks.llm: The LLM answers from the context, with citations.

dives: Chunk size?
300-800 tokens with overlap; keep source, date and ACL as metadata.
Why hybrid search plus rerank?
Vectors catch meaning, keywords catch exact terms; the reranker orders them.
How do you stop made-up answers?
Answer only from context, cite, say 'not found'.
How do you measure it?
Recall@k for retrieval, faithfulness for answers.
wrap: Bottleneck: retrieval quality. Fix: better chunking, rerank, evals.
Next: agentic RAG, multi-hop questions.

reqF: Ask a human before risky actions
est: A task = 10-50 model calls + tool calls
Long tasks: minutes, so run asynchronously
data: tasks + steps (state, tool calls, results)
memory: vector + key-value

blocks.ag: The orchestrator runs plan, act, observe.
blocks.llm: The model plans the next step.
blocks.mem: Memory to recall and save facts.

dives: How does the loop stop?
Step and token limits, a done check, timeouts.
How do tools stay safe?
Least-privilege permissions, approval for risky ones, sandbox.
Failures mid-task?
Persist state per step, make tools idempotent, resume.
How do you know it works?
Task-success evals and traces.
wrap: Bottleneck: long tasks and cost. Fix: smaller models for sub-steps, caching.
Next: multi-agent, scheduled agents.

reqF: Take a coding task from the terminal or IDE
reqN: Never break the repo: verify before commit
est: Context is the scarce resource: load only what matters
api: Tool calls: read, edit, grep, shell, git, MCP
data: project memory file loaded every session
session transcript and checkpoints

blocks.ag: The agent loop: gather context, act, verify.
blocks.llm: The model decides the next action.
blocks.sh: Shell sandbox runs tests and builds.
blocks.mcp: MCP servers bring issues and docs.
blocks.git: Commit and open a pull request.

dives: How does it find the right code?
Search first (grep, file tree), then read only what matters.
How do you keep it safe?
Permission modes, sandboxed shell, never push without asking.
How do you know the change works?
Run tests and build before commit.
Big tasks?
Sub-agents search in parallel, each with its own context.
wrap: Bottleneck: context window. Fix: search tools, summaries, sub-agents.
Next: CI integration, code review bots.

reqF: Search the web and internal docs
reqN: Budget on steps, tokens and time
est: One question ≈ 3-6 sub-questions x 10 searches each
Tokens per report: hundreds of thousands
data: plan, sub-questions, findings with source URLs
final report

blocks.u: The user asks a big question.
blocks.w2: Each has its own context window.
blocks.rep: The writer turns findings into a cited report.

dives: Why multiple agents?
Parallel search, separate contexts, faster and broader.
How do findings come back?
Compressed summaries with sources, not raw pages.
How do you control cost?
Budgets on steps, tokens and time per agent.
Quality?
Every claim must cite; check citations before the final report.
wrap: Bottleneck: tokens. Fix: smaller models for search, compression.
Next: follow-up questions, saved research.

reqF: Answer customers from the help centre
reqN: Safe: limits on actions like refunds
data: conversations, actions taken, outcome, CSAT

blocks.c: Customers write in by chat or email.
blocks.ag: The support agent decides: answer, act or escalate.
blocks.kb: Answers grounded in the help centre.
blocks.crm: Tools on orders and CRM, with limits.
blocks.h: A human takes over with full context.

dives: How do you keep answers right?
Ground in the help centre with RAG; cite articles.
How do you limit damage?
Tool limits like a refund cap, approval above it.
When to escalate?
Low confidence, angry customer, or asked for a human.
How do you measure it?
Resolution rate, CSAT, escalation rate.
wrap: Bottleneck: hard cases. Fix: better handoff, learn from human replies.
Next: voice channel, proactive messages.

reqF: Talk to callers on the phone or web
Understand and answer in natural speech
est: Latency budget: STT ~200 ms + LLM ~300 ms + TTS ~200 ms + network
api: SIP / WebRTC audio in and out
Tool calls: book, look up customer
data: call records, transcripts, audio for evals

blocks.rtc: WebRTC or SIP gateway carries audio.
blocks.ag: The voice agent (LLM) decides what to say.

dives: How do you hit 800 ms?
Stream every stage: STT partials, LLM tokens, TTS audio.
Interruptions?
Voice activity detection stops TTS when the caller talks.
Slow tools?
Short filler phrases while the tool runs.
Speech-to-speech models?
Fewer hops and lower latency, less control.
wrap: Bottleneck: latency. Fix: colocate models, stream, smaller models.
Next: multilingual, call analytics.

reqF: One endpoint for every team's model calls
est: Thousands of requests per second across teams
Billions of tokens a month: chargeback matters
data: teams, keys, quotas
usage events: tokens, cost, model, latency

blocks.apps: Internal apps and agents call one gateway.
blocks.g: Guardrails and PII redaction before providers.
blocks.obs: Tracing and cost metering per team.

dives: Why one gateway?
One place for keys, quotas, safety and cost.
Routing?
By cost, latency and capability, with fallback.
Data protection?
Redact PII before it leaves; log what was sent.
Chargeback?
Meter tokens and cost per team key.
wrap: Bottleneck: the gateway itself. Fix: stateless, horizontally scaled.
Next: evals, prompt registry.
